title: I am as My servant thinks
word: I am as My servant thinks
hook: Allah says, I am as My servant thinks of Me (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday, hadith qudsi, and your line: allah said, he said. Did you catch who was really speaking in something passed along? Day one thousand one hundred fifty-eight.

Two people get the same voicemail from a doctor's office: please call us back. One spends the afternoon sure it's bad news, rehearsing every outcome. The other assumes it's about rescheduling, and makes lunch. Same message. Two very different afternoons. What a person expects shapes the day they live. Yesterday we met the sacred hadith, the reports in which the Prophet relates words from Allah. Today, one of them, and it's about expecting. Today's word is a whole sentence: I am as My servant thinks.
screen: `THE SAME VOICEMAIL.` → `TWO DIFFERENT AFTERNOONS.` → `A SACRED HADITH ABOUT EXPECTING.`

segments.voice: First, the line. In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ relates that Allah says: I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. It's short, and it says a great deal. In this report, Allah ties the way He meets a person to what that person expects of Him. Second, the name for it. Scholars call this husn al-zann billah, thinking well of Allah: expecting mercy, forgiveness, an answer. And it isn't only for easy days. In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet tells his companions that none of them should die except while thinking well of Allah. So this expectation is meant to last to the very end. Third, the balance. Commentators on this hadith add a careful note: thinking well of Allah isn't the same as assuming nothing matters. They pair hope with effort. A person thinks well of Allah while praying, while repenting, while trying. A student who studies and hopes for a good grade is thinking well. A student who skips every class and hopes is only guessing. Fourth, the next lines. The same report goes on: if he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself, and if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than it. Remembering runs both ways. And after that, the report keeps going, into a picture of distance and of speed. That picture is tomorrow's.
screen: `I AM AS MY SERVANT THINKS OF ME.` · `THINKING WELL OF ALLAH, TO THE END.` · `HOPE THAT WALKS WITH EFFORT.` · `REMEMBERING RUNS BOTH WAYS.`

segments.voice: The practice: think well of Allah. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one thing that's worrying you right now. Hold it gently. Notice what you've been expecting about it. Maybe the worst; maybe nothing at all. Now, without pretending the worry isn't real, try the other way of expecting. If you believe, try meeting it expecting Allah's mercy. If you're not sure what you believe, simply try expecting that some good can still come of it. Breathe in on the worry. Breathe out on the better expectation. Don't force anything. The bell holds the time.
I am as My servant thinks. A sacred hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari: Allah meets a person as that person expects of Him. Today's word.
screen: `I AM AS MY SERVANT THINKS — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: think well of him. Today, when your mind jumps straight to the worst, catch it once and try the other expectation. Tomorrow: draw near a span. Day one thousand one hundred fifty-eight.

howItsDone: Muslims may recall this hadith in times of worry or illness, and scholars teach thinking well of Allah as hope joined to prayer, repentance and effort.

fork.setup: a friend says: 'if Allah is as I think, I'll just assume He's fine with whatever I do.' what do the commentators on this hadith say?
options: thinking well of Allah goes with prayer, repentance and effort.
you should never hope for anything.
fork.reveal: hope walks with effort. the student who studies and hopes is thinking well; the one who skips class and hopes is guessing.

original.note: good opinion, thinking well: husn al-zann billah is thinking well of Allah.

trapdoor: what you thought: think positive, and it'll all work out.
what it means: Allah meets a person as that person expects of Him, so expect His mercy.
what a scholar hears: husn al-zann billah, hope held to the very end, and always paired with effort.

notes: Bukhari 7405 (I am as My servant thinks of Me; I am with him when he remembers Me; remembering in himself / in a gathering): confirm number; paraphrased. The span/cubit lines of the same report are left for day 1159.

Muslim 2877 (none of you should die except thinking well of Allah, narrated by Jabir): confirm number; the detail that it was said shortly before the Prophet's death is left out under the claims rule.
'Commentators pair hope with effort' summarizes the classical commentary (e.g. Ibn Hajar, al-Nawawi) on this hadith; confirm phrasing.
Term husn al-zann billah: confirm transliteration and Arabic (حسن الظن).
Practice addresses believers and the unsure separately and requires no prayer; the hook's doctor's-office image is an everyday example, not a medical claim.
Editor: 'it's startling if you sit with it' changed to 'it says a great deal' so the narrator doesn't tell the listener how the line will feel.
